results.name: Resistance Band Calf Press Sitting on Chair
instructions: Sit on a chair with your back straight, knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat hovering just above the floor. Loop a resistance band around your forefeet, holding the ends of the band with your hands.
Extend your forefeet downward to point your toes to the floor, pressing against the resistance of the band to engage your calf muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, flexing your forefeet back towards you.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning forward.
Keep your hands steady to ensure consistent tension in the band.
Exhale as you press your toes forward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Resistance Band Calf Press Sitting on Chair is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins, Hamstrings.

results.name: Resistance Band Clam
instructions: Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Lie on your side with your legs bent at a 90-degree angle and your feet stacked together.
Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on the floor for stability.
Keeping your feet together, lift your top knee as high as you can without moving your pelvis or back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your knee to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Keep your feet together to ensure proper form and muscle activation.
Exhale as you lift your knee and inhale as you lower it back down.
Ensure your head and neck remain aligned with your spine for comfort.
results.description: Resistance Band Clam is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Resistance Band Hip Thrust (Version 2)
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a loop resistance band firmly under your heels and pass it over your thighs close to your hips. Keep your hands extended by your sides with hands firm on the floor.
Engage your core and glutes, and lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the bridge position for a moment, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your lower back; keep a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Focus on engaging your glutes throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your hips and press your knees outward, and inhale as you bring your knees back together and lower your hips .
results.description: Resistance Band Hip Thrust (Version 2) is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Hamstrings, Abductors.

results.name: Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees
instructions: Kneel on the floor with a loop resistance band anchored at a low point behind you and wrapped around your hips. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Sit back on your heels, ensuring the resistance band remains taut.
Thrust your hips forward, coming up onto your knees and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you thrust your hips forward and inhale as you sit back on your heels.
Ensure the resistance band stays securely anchored behind you to maintain consistent tension.
Focus on engaging your glutes throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Abductors.

results.name: Resistance Band Kneeling Leg Half Circle on Bench
instructions: Start in a tabletop position on a bench, with your hands holding the edges for support and your knees under your hips. Attach a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Lift your right leg off the bench and extend it straight back, keeping it under bench level.
Move your right leg in a half-circle motion inward over your left leg until it comes in level with the bench, keeping the resistance band taut.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Exhale as you move your leg in the half-circle motion and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Keep your shoulders and hips squared to the floor.
Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Kneeling Leg Half Circle on Bench is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Core, Lower Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Leg Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a loop resistance band around your ankles. Arms are hanging by your sides.
Bend your right knee and curl your right leg towards your glutes, keeping your thigh stationary.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control, fully extending it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Exhale as you curl your leg up and inhale as you extend it back down.
Maintain a slight bend in your standing leg for balance.
Focus on engaging your hamstrings throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Leg Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

results.name: Resistance Band Leg Kickback
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips. Place a loop resistance band under your right foot and hold the other end on the floor with your right hand.
Kick your right leg backward until it's parallel to the floor, extending it fully while keeping the resistance band taut.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Exhale as you kick your leg back and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Ensure the resistance band stays securely under your foot and hand to maintain consistent tension.
Focus on engaging your glutes throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Leg Kickback is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Resistance Band Lying Abduction
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight up towards the ceiling and a loop resistance band around your ankles. Place your arms by your sides on the floor for stability.
Engage your core and keep your legs straight and feet flexed.
Open your legs wide apart against the resistance of the band, keeping your legs straight and maintaining control.
Slowly bring your legs back together to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you open your legs and inhale as you bring them back together.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension on the muscles.
Focus on engaging your hip abductors and glute muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Lying Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.

results.name: Resistance Band Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms by your sides and a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your legs extended and together.
Engage your core to lift your right leg straight up towards the ceiling, keeping the resistance band taut and your left leg flat on the floor.
Slowly lower your leg back down with control, stopping just before your heel touches the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to lifting your left leg.
tips: Focus on engaging your abdominals throughout the movement.
Avoid lifting your lower back off the floor; keep it pressed down for the duration of the exercise.
Maintain a slight bend in your knee if necessary to reduce strain.
results.description: Resistance Band Lying Leg Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals.

results.name: Resistance Band One Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a loop resistance band around your right thigh, just above your knee, and loop it under your right forefoot.
Press through your right heel to lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, while keeping your left leg bent off the floor.
Hold the bridge position for a second, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hamstrings throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
results.description: Resistance Band One Leg Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Hamstrings, Core.
